holidays.name: National Hot Fudge Sundae Day
holidays.description: A day to pile warm, gooey chocolate fudge over cold ice cream. Add whipped cream, nuts and a cherry if you like. The hot-and-cold contrast is the whole point, so don't let it melt while you decide.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial food observance, and its founder is unclear. It honors the classic soda-fountain sundae. One popular legend credits a Hollywood confectioner, C.C. Brown, with serving the first hot fudge sundae in the early 1900s.
holidays.funFact: The hot fudge sundae is a showdown of temperatures. The fudge is served hot enough to start melting the ice cream on contact, so speed eating is part of the tradition.

holidays.name: National Water Gun Fight Day
holidays.description: A summer-heat excuse to soak your friends, family and neighbors with squirt guns, water balloons and anything else that sprays. Dry clothes are optional. Sneak attacks are encouraged.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial summer observance. It was placed in late July, when the weather is hot enough to make a surprise soaking welcome.
holidays.funFact: The Super Soaker, the most famous water blaster ever made, was invented by Lonnie Johnson, an engineer who worked on NASA space missions. He came up with the idea while tinkering with a bathroom experiment.

holidays.name: Merry-Go-Round Day
holidays.description: A day to climb aboard a painted pony and go in circles for the sheer joy of it. Nostalgia, calliope music and a bit of dizziness are all part of the fun.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It celebrates the carousel, a fairground favorite for generations.
holidays.funFact: Carousels in the United States usually spin counterclockwise, while many in the United Kingdom and Europe turn clockwise.
